MAD18.author: Madras, David and Pitassi, Toni and Zemel, Richard
MAD18.title: Predict responsibly: Improving fairness and accuracy by learning to defer
MAD18.howpublished: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 31
MAD18.apa: Madras, D., Pitassi, T., & Zemel, R. (2018). Predict responsibly: Improving fairness and accuracy by learning to defer. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 31*. https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2018/hash/09d37c08f7b129e96277388757530c72-Abstract.html
MAD18.method: Predict/defer learning with a fallible downstream decision maker and fairness-sensitive loss.
MAD18.implication: Human-versus-AI expected loss is prior art; no retry benchmark is replicated here.
MAD18.locator: Instance features; prediction or deferral; reported classification evaluation.

MOZ20.author: Mozannar, Hussein and Sontag, David
MOZ20.title: Consistent estimators for learning to defer to an expert
MOZ20.apa: Mozannar, H., & Sontag, D. (2020). Consistent estimators for learning to defer to an expert. *Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, 119*, 7076-7087. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/mozannar20b.html
MOZ20.method: Cost-sensitive reduction and consistent surrogate learning; Bayes decisions compare machine and expert conditional correctness.
MOZ20.implication: HandoffX reuses the decision principle, not the trained surrogate or its sample guarantees.
MOZ20.locator: Original PDF pp. 2-4, displayed Bayes rules and loss; equation pages visually inspected.

VER22.author: Verma, Rajeev and Nalisnick, Eric
VER22.title: Calibrated learning to defer with one-vs-all classifiers
VER22.apa: Verma, R., & Nalisnick, E. (2022). Calibrated learning to defer with one-vs-all classifiers. *Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, 162*, 22184-22202. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/verma22c.html
VER22.method: One-vs-all construction addresses calibration of expert correctness in learning to defer.
VER22.implication: Numerically valid probabilities are not automatically calibrated; HandoffX does not fit an estimator.
VER22.locator: Official PMLR abstract and complete metadata.

VER23.author: Verma, Rajeev and Barrejon, Daniel and Nalisnick, Eric
VER23.title: Learning to defer to multiple experts: Consistent surrogate losses, confidence calibration, and conformal ensembles
VER23.apa: Verma, R., Barrejon, D., & Nalisnick, E. (2023). Learning to defer to multiple experts: Consistent surrogate losses, confidence calibration, and conformal ensembles. *Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, 206*, 11415-11434. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v206/verma23a.html
VER23.method: Multiple-expert deferral, calibrated surrogate scores and conformal expert ensembles.
VER23.implication: Multiple candidate helpers or expert uncertainty are not inherently new.
VER23.locator: Official PMLR abstract; no independent proof replication.

CHA22.author: Charusaie, Mohammad-Amin and Mozannar, Hussein and Sontag, David and Samadi, Samira
CHA22.title: Sample efficient learning of predictors that complement humans
CHA22.apa: Charusaie, M., Mozannar, H., Sontag, D., & Samadi, S. (2022). Sample efficient learning of predictors that complement humans. *Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, 162*, 2972-3005. https://proceedings.mlr.press/v162/charusaie22a.html
CHA22.method: Sample-efficient learning of predictors that complement human decisions.
CHA22.implication: Human complementarity and data acquisition require their own learning evaluation.

HEM23.author: Hemmer, Patrick and Thede, Lukas and Vössing, Michael and Jakubik, Johannes and Kühl, Niklas
HEM23.title: Learning to defer with limited expert predictions
HEM23.howpublished: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 37(5), 6002–6011
HEM23.apa: Hemmer, P., Thede, L., Vössing, M., Jakubik, J., & Kühl, N. (2023). Learning to defer with limited expert predictions. *Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 37*(5), 6002-6011. https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v37i5.25742
HEM23.method: Expertise prediction supplies missing expert predictions from limited labeled examples.
HEM23.implication: Limited human labels are established research; correction: Lukas Thede, not Lars.
HEM23.locator: Official AAAI authors/abstract; real and synthetic expert evaluations reported.

IYE05.author: Iyengar, Garud N.
IYE05.title: Robust dynamic programming
IYE05.apa: Iyengar, G. N. (2005). Robust dynamic programming. *Mathematics of Operations Research, 30*(2), 257-280. https://doi.org/10.1287/moor.1040.0129
IYE05.method: Robust dynamic programming uses structured uncertainty sets to support dynamic recursion.
IYE05.implication: Rectangularity is consequential; HandoffX claims an envelope, not fixed-parameter minimax equivalence.
IYE05.locator: Publisher record/abstract; full original proof not independently rechecked.

NIL05.author: Nilim, Arnab and El Ghaoui, Laurent
NIL05.title: Robust control of Markov decision processes with uncertain transition matrices
NIL05.apa: Nilim, A., & El Ghaoui, L. (2005). Robust control of Markov decision processes with uncertain transition matrices. *Operations Research, 53*(5), 780-798. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.1050.0216
NIL05.method: Robust MDP control handles uncertain transition matrices.
NIL05.implication: Uncertain action transitions and worst-case cost optimization are established.
NIL05.locator: Publisher record/abstract; exact assumptions not re-proved from original paper.

SUI20.author: Suilen, Marnix and Jansen, Nils and Cubuktepe, Murat and Topcu, Ufuk
SUI20.title: Robust policy synthesis for uncertain POMDPs via convex optimization
SUI20.howpublished: Proceedings of the Twenty-Ninth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 4113–4120
SUI20.apa: Suilen, M., Jansen, N., Cubuktepe, M., & Topcu, U. (2020). Robust policy synthesis for uncertain POMDPs via convex optimization. *Proceedings of the Twenty-Ninth International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence* (pp. 4113-4120). https://doi.org/10.24963/ijcai.2020/569
SUI20.method: Uncertain-POMDP policy synthesis via convex optimization.
SUI20.implication: Partial observation plus transition uncertainty is prior art.
SUI20.locator: Official IJCAI abstract/metadata; not an implemented algorithm comparison.

CUB21.author: Cubuktepe, Murat and Jansen, Nils and Junges, Sebastian and Marandi, Ahmadreza and Suilen, Marnix and Topcu, Ufuk
CUB21.title: Robust finite-state controllers for uncertain POMDPs
CUB21.howpublished: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 35(13), 11792–11800
CUB21.apa: Cubuktepe, M., Jansen, N., Junges, S., Marandi, A., Suilen, M., & Topcu, U. (2021). Robust finite-state controllers for uncertain POMDPs. *Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 35*(13), 11792-11800. https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v35i13.17401
CUB21.method: Robust finite-state controllers for uncertain POMDPs and specified objectives.
CUB21.implication: HandoffX does not reproduce this controller-synthesis algorithm or inherit all guarantees.
CUB21.locator: Official AAAI metadata/abstract; CDN PDF access failed.

ROS11.author: Rosenthal, Stephanie and Veloso, Manuela and Dey, Anind
ROS11.title: Learning accuracy and availability of humans who help mobile robots
ROS11.howpublished: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 25(1), 1501–1506
ROS11.apa: Rosenthal, S., Veloso, M., & Dey, A. (2011). Learning accuracy and availability of humans who help mobile robots. *Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 25*(1), 1501-1506. https://doi.org/10.1609/aaai.v25i1.7980
ROS11.method: Robot assistance decisions model human accuracy and availability.
ROS11.implication: Imperfect or unavailable people are established, not a new HandoffX concept.

SIN23.author: Singi, Siddharth and He, Zhanpeng and Pan, Alvin and Patel, Sandip and Sigurdsson, Gunnar A. and Piramuthu, Robinson and Song, Shuran and Ciocarlie, Matei
SIN23.title: Decision making for human-in-the-loop robotic agents via uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning
SIN23.apa: Singi, S., He, Z., Pan, A., Patel, S., Sigurdsson, G. A., Piramuthu, R., Song, S., & Ciocarlie, M. (2023). *Decision making for human-in-the-loop robotic agents via uncertainty-aware reinforcement learning* (Version 2). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2303.06710
SIN23.method: HULA queries an expert using estimated return variance with a limited call budget.
SIN23.implication: Original method assumes consistently high-quality advice; this prototype permits weak helpers.
SIN23.locator: HTML section III and evaluation overview; robotic expert returns an action, not terminal rescue.

GHO24.author: Ghoummaid, Marah and Shalit, Uri
GHO24.title: When to act and when to ask: Policy learning with deferral under hidden confounding
GHO24.howpublished: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 37
GHO24.apa: Ghoummaid, M., & Shalit, U. (2024). When to act and when to ask: Policy learning with deferral under hidden confounding. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 37*. https://doi.org/10.52202/079017-1785
GHO24.method: Policy learning with deferral accounts for hidden confounding.
GHO24.implication: Observed outcomes do not identify missing human/AI counterfactuals without assumptions.
GHO24.locator: Official NeurIPS abstract; no causal estimator is implemented here.

JIT23.author: Jitkrittum, Wittawat and Gupta, Neha and Menon, Aditya Krishna and Narasimhan, Harikrishna and Rawat, Ankit Singh and Kumar, Sanjiv
JIT23.title: When does confidence-based cascade deferral suffice?
JIT23.howpublished: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 36
JIT23.apa: Jitkrittum, W., Gupta, N., Menon, A. K., Narasimhan, H., Rawat, A. S., & Kumar, S. (2023). When does confidence-based cascade deferral suffice?. *Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 36*. https://doi.org/10.52202/075280-0431
JIT23.method: Characterizes when confidence-only cascade deferral fails, including specialist downstream models and shift.
JIT23.implication: A scalar AI-confidence threshold need not be sufficient.
JIT23.locator: Official NeurIPS abstract; experiments reported by authors, not rerun.

SHA26.author: Shaikh, Nadeem
SHA26.title: Knowing when to ask for help: Bayesian self-escalation in hierarchical LLM agents
SHA26.howpublished: arXiv. arXiv version 1; manuscript labeled Version 1.1
SHA26.apa: Shaikh, N. (2026). *Knowing when to ask for help: Bayesian self-escalation in hierarchical LLM agents* (arXiv version 1; manuscript Version 1.1). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2608.24087
SHA26.method: Bayesian intra-generation stopping, learned competence posterior and stronger-model escalation.
SHA26.implication: Timing/calibration are prior art; reported real-model validation does not execute the optimal stopping DP.
SHA26.locator: arXiv v1 HTML sections 3-5, 8, 10; internal Version 1.1 is not arXiv v2.

HIL26.author: Trinh, Tu and Elfeki, Mohamed and Luo, Guangze and Luu, Kelvin and Hunt, Nathan and Hernández, Ernesto and Marwaha, Nandan and He, Yannis Yiming and Wang, Charles and Carabedo, Fernando and Castillo, Alessa and Liu, Bing
HIL26.title: HiL-Bench (Human-in-Loop Benchmark): Do agents know when to ask for help?
HIL26.apa: Trinh, T., Elfeki, M., Luo, G., Luu, K., Hunt, N., Hernández, E., Marwaha, N., He, Y. Y., Wang, C., Carabedo, F., Castillo, A., & Liu, B. (2026). *HiL-Bench (Human-in-Loop Benchmark): Do agents know when to ask for help?* (Version 4). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2604.09408
HIL26.method: Progressive blockers and asking behavior in coding/SQL, evaluated with Ask-F1 and task outcomes.
HIL26.implication: Sequential help-seeking benchmarks already exist; HandoffX instead isolates a costed synthetic decision model.
HIL26.locator: Version 4 HTML design/limitations; corrected author list and order.

ALV25.author: Alves, Jean V. and Leitão, Diogo and Jesus, Sérgio and Sampaio, Marco O. P. and Liébana, Javier and Saleiro, Pedro and Figueiredo, Mário A. T. and Bizarro, Pedro
ALV25.title: A benchmarking framework and dataset for learning to defer in human-AI decision-making
ALV25.apa: Alves, J. V., Leitão, D., Jesus, S., Sampaio, M. O. P., Liébana, J., Saleiro, P., Figueiredo, M. A. T., & Bizarro, P. (2025). A benchmarking framework and dataset for learning to defer in human-AI decision-making. *Scientific Data, 12*, Article 506. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-025-04664-y
ALV25.method: Learning-to-defer benchmark includes synthetic expert behavior and capacity constraints.
ALV25.implication: Benchmarking fallible humans is established; its tabular allocation task differs from repeated recoveries.
ALV25.locator: PMC full text methods/limitations; synthetic experts are not real participants.

ANG24.author: Angelopoulos, Anastasios N. and Bates, Stephen and Fisch, Adam and Lei, Lihua and Schuster, Tal
ANG24.title: Conformal risk control
ANG24.apa: Angelopoulos, A. N., Bates, S., Fisch, A., Lei, L., & Schuster, T. (2024). Conformal risk control. *International Conference on Learning Representations*. https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/f3549ef9b5ff520a7e41ff3cc306ab2b-Abstract-Conference.html
ANG24.method: Conformal risk control bounds expected monotone losses under its calibration assumptions.
ANG24.implication: The implemented guard is a union bound, not conformal risk control or distribution-free certification.
ANG24.locator: Official ICLR abstract; no conformal implementation or guarantee claimed.

YAO25.author: Yao, Shunyu and Shinn, Noah and Razavi, Pedram and Narasimhan, Karthik
YAO25.title: τ-bench: A benchmark for tool-agent-user interaction in real-world domains
YAO25.apa: Yao, S., Shinn, N., Razavi, P., & Narasimhan, K. (2025). τ-bench: A benchmark for tool-agent-user interaction in real-world domains. *International Conference on Learning Representations*. https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/1b126cc38b8638e07bef37e7b2bb72bf-Abstract-Conference.html
YAO25.method: Tool-agent-user benchmark evaluates interactions in operational domains.
YAO25.implication: Real agent interaction is broader than the toy simulator; no benchmark result is reproduced.

BAL23.author: Balazadeh, Vahid and De, Abir and Singla, Adish and Gomez-Rodriguez, Manuel
BAL23.title: Learning to switch among agents in a team via 2-layer Markov decision processes
BAL23.apa: Balazadeh, V., De, A., Singla, A., & Gomez-Rodriguez, M. (2023). *Learning to switch among agents in a team via 2-layer Markov decision processes* (Version 3). arXiv. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2002.04258
BAL23.method: Two-layer MDP switches control among agents, with confidence bounds and reported sublinear regret.
BAL23.implication: Switching and shared environment information are prior art; no new online-regret claim is made.
BAL23.locator: arXiv v3 record; final TMLR record blocked, so cite this version.

KAE98.author: Kaelbling, Leslie Pack and Littman, Michael L. and Cassandra, Anthony R.
KAE98.title: Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
KAE98.apa: Kaelbling, L. P., Littman, M. L., & Cassandra, A. R. (1998). Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains. *Artificial Intelligence, 101*(1-2), 99-134. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0004-3702(98)00023-X
KAE98.method: Belief-state control in partially observable stochastic environments.
KAE98.implication: The finite count-state solver is a restricted POMDP specialization.
KAE98.locator: Publisher metadata verified; author-hosted PDF timed out.

ROSS11.author: Ross, Stéphane and Pineau, Joelle and Chaib-draa, Brahim and Kreitmann, Pierre
ROSS11.title: A Bayesian approach for learning and planning in partially observable Markov decision processes
ROSS11.apa: Ross, S., Pineau, J., Chaib-draa, B., & Kreitmann, P. (2011). A Bayesian approach for learning and planning in partially observable Markov decision processes. *Journal of Machine Learning Research, 12*, 1729-1770. https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v12/ross11a.html
ROSS11.method: Bayes-adaptive POMDPs jointly track state and uncertain model parameters.
ROSS11.implication: Joint hidden-state/parameter beliefs and information-sensitive planning are established.
ROSS11.locator: JMLR PDF sections 2-3; selected equations inspected; p. 1736 screenshot inspected.
